messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: runtime-prod - significant latency/throughput regression after recent canary roll (deploy id=canary-2026-03-17). 95p latency > 3s in us-west, kernel fallback events spiking. Paging on-call.

alice: ack. I'm on it — pulling logs and KV cache stats.

ben: seeing a swarm of kernel_fallback events on the canary hosts:
```
2026-03-17T21:10:05Z ERROR kernel_fallback: fallback_triggered=true reason=eviction pressure=0.82
2026-03-17T21:10:06Z WARN batcher: batch_window_spike=120ms qlen=98
```

alice: matches traces — throughput per-instance dropped ~40% at 21:09. Prefetch/paging thrash + continuous batching seems to amplify latencies.

carla: @alice @ben any customer-facing errors? support-ops reported increased 502s?

support-ops: Confirmed. Seeing a spike in 502/504 for /v1/generate for a subset of mid-tier customers (about 8% of requests in last 5m). Open ticket #INC-4521.

sam: stackdriver/metrics shows KV cache eviction rate up x6 on canary pool, memory compaction kicking in. Might be a regression in the new allocation heuristic.

ben: reproducing locally when we enable the new allocation path + extended batch window. This looks like the canary introduced aggressive batching that holds KV caches longer -> eviction -> kernel fallback.

alice: agreed. Immediate mitigation options: 1) toggle kill-switch to disable new batching heuristic for canary; 2) rollback canary; 3) emergency kernel affinity tweak. Quickest is kill-switch. Any objections?

dave: +1 to kill-switch first. Rolling back will take longer and may cause traffic churn.

carla: I'm taking handoff in 10m (on-call rotation). If kill-switch fixes visible impact, we can avoid rollback. Provide concise playbook for the handoff.

ben: commands I ran:
```bash
# disable new batching heuristic (global flag for canary pool)
deployctl flags set runtime.batchheuristic.canary false --pool canary-2026
# verify flag state
deployctl flags get runtime.batchheuristic.canary --pool canary-2026
```
Result: flag flip acknowledged by agents within ~12s.

alice: after flip: observed kernel_fallback events drop by ~70% and 95p latency down from 3.2s -> 1.1s within 90s. Throughput recovering to baseline. Support reports 502s decreasing.

support-ops: Customer impact trending down. Noticing some latency tail still elevated for a small subset. Monitoring.

carla: Good. Can you capture timeline and artifacts for postmortem? I want: canary commit id, flag diff, kernel logs, batcher traces, customer list impacted, and timelines. I'll coordinate a rollback only if metrics don't normalize in 15m.

sam: capturing KV cache heap profiles and a heapdiff. Uploading to GCS: gs://redwood-incidents/INC-4521/heap_2026-03-17.tar.gz

ben: also chopped a quick command to revert canary if needed: `deployctl rollout revert canary-2026-03-17 --reason "kernel fallback regression"` — takes ~6-8m to fully drain.

dave: Once carla takes over, I'll start drafting a partial customer communication for affected customers (apology + mitigation steps + ETA for full resolution).

carla: taking over now. Summary: kill-switch flipped, immediate metrics improved, remaining tail latency small but decreasing. Action items:
- Ben: collect and attach logs + batcher config diffs to INC-4521.
- Alice: run a focused smoke load against a canary host to confirm stability for next 30m.
- Sam: continue KV heap profiling.
- Dave: draft customer comms and post initial note to #support.
- Support-ops: keep ticket updated and collect customer request ids for follow-ups.

carla: If after 15m tail doesn't recover fully, we'll perform a controlled rollback. If it stays healthy, we'll keep flag disabled and schedule a postmortem and a patch to the allocation heuristic.

alice: smoke test started: sending steady 200rps for 10m to canary host group. Early signs: p95 ~ 350ms, p99 950ms (improved). Will update.

incident-bot: Incident INC-4521 created, sev=2, assigned=carla, link=https://incidents.redwood.ai/INC-4521

carla: marking on-call handoff complete. Monitoring channel and will poke if we need to escalate. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
